newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-VENABLES CONFIRMED AS AUSTRALIA'S COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VENABLES CONFIRMED AS AUSTRALIA'S COACH.

text.p: Former England coach Terry Venables on Tuesday confirmed that he has agreed to become the new team boss of Australia.
The news was announced by the 53-year-old Venables at his west London club Scribes.

Under the terms of the reputed 200,000 pounds ($334,000) a year deal, a third more than he received from his England post, Venables will take up his new role on January 1 but will retain his position as director of football at Portsmouth.

But the one-time Crystal Palace, QPR, Barcelona and Tottenham manager will spend around four months of the year in Australia with the rest of his time spent traversing Europe keeping an eye on the growing number of Australian stars playing on the continent.
Asked whether he thought he could take Australia to the World Cup finals, Venables said: "I sincerely hope so, I wouldn't have taken it if I didn't think I could.
"That's got to be the target. I've got to work out how to get to the target, that's my job."
Asked if he would feel safe walking down the street if Australia played England, he quipped: "I never have before, I don't know why I would start now.
"I think it's a possibility, but there are many permutations of what could happen."
Asked why he had taken the job, Venables said: "I think that what interested me was international football again. I've had two and a half years with England, and I really did enjoy it.
"I don't regret the decision that I made, after negotiations with the F.A., but there was a frustration, and I would have liked to have finished the job properly to go to the World Cup.
"Now I have a chance to make that happen, and I'll do my damnedest to do that."

Ambitious Soccer Australia chairman David Hill finally persuaded Venables to take the job, a week after it emerged that he headed the shortlist after long-term coach Eddie Thomson quit last month to join Japanese J-League side Hiroshima.
Venables stood down from the England post in June, after his side were a penalty shoot-out away from reaching the final of Euro 96.

He has been linked with a number of club management jobs both at home and abroad, including Blackburn and a number of European sides, but admitted that the challenge of a return to the international stage was one which attracted him.
Venables' task will be to steer the Socceroos to the World Cup finals in France in 1998, the job he had originally been appointed to achieve with England.
Australia, whose only previous finals appearance came in 1974, must win the Oceania qualifying section and then a play-off with the fourth team in Asia to reach France.
